title: Germanys AfD hits record poll numbers
text:
RT.com
27 Mar 2025, 02:51 GMT+10
The right-wing party is polling just 3.5% beyond Germanys top conservative CDU/CSU alliance, a new INSA poll shows
The right-wing Alternative for Germany (AfD) party has achieved a record high in public support polls conducted by Germany's leading Institute for New Social Answers (INSA) pollster.
The latest poll, released by INSA on Tuesday, indicated 23.5% support for the party, while the top conservative alliance, Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and its sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), polled at 27%. The figure constituted a 1.5% drop since the CDU/CSU achieved a victory in Germany's general election on February 23.
"This is the highest value ever measured for the AfD in the INSA opinion trend," the head of INSA, Hermann Binkert, told Bild daily.
The AfD gained nearly three points in polls since the election and is currently just 3.5% behind the CDU/CSU alliance. The CSU alone polled at 21%, with its sister party fetching a further 7% for the alliance, Binkert noted.
The INSA poll sampled opinions of some 2,004 respondents, representing various social groups of Germany.
According to pollster estimates, the party's public support could reach as high as 30.5%. Other parties, however, still maintain higher estimated ceilings, with the CDU/CSU theoretically able to reach up to 42%, while the centrist-left Social Democratic Party (SDP) could get up to 39.5%, according to INSA's analysts.
The CDU/CSU emerged as the strongest force in last month's parliamentary election with 28.5% of the vote, albeit failing to get a majority. The party is currently in coalition talks with the SPD, which suffered a crushing defeat with the record-low 16.4% during the election. Should the two forces reach a coalition, however, they would hold 328 seats in the Bundestag, comfortably surpassing the 316-seat mark to get a majority.
The AfD secured a solid second place during the election, receiving 20.8% of the vote - a twofold rise from the 10.4% they got in 2021. Despite the result, the party remains ostracized by the other major political forces that refuse to somehow cooperate with it, and is commonly labeled 'far-right' by officials and media alike.
(RT.com)
